key_insight: Distill a model's own multi-step generative trajectories into a compact few-step diffusion decoder, and use direct discriminative optimization to preserve final-output quality — enabling fast parallel token generation with far fewer refinement steps.
problem_solved: Diffusion LLMs need many iterative refinement steps for high-quality text, making inference slow; cutting steps drastically reduces generation quality. The paper tackles improving few-step decoding quality without expensive inference.
method: Trajectory self-distillation: record high-quality multi-step generative trajectories from the teacher (same model or long-run sampler) and train a student to emulate the effective mapping in far fewer steps.

Direct discriminative optimization: optimize a discriminative objective focused on final output quality (rather than only reconstruction of intermediate states) so the few-step model produces better end results.
Joint training/inference design that preserves parallel token decoding while minimizing the number of refinement steps needed for acceptable fluency and fidelity.
impact: Enables practical, low-latency deployment of diffusion-based language models by maintaining quality with dramatically fewer refinement steps — useful for real-time applications and cost-sensitive inference.
visual_elements: Trajectory diagram: long multi-step diffusion path vs. compressed few-step distilled path, highlighting removed steps.
Bar/line chart: quality (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity) and latency trade-off across step counts, showing improved few-step performance with T3D.
Training flowchart: collect trajectories → distillation loss + discriminative objective → student few-step model.
Icons: parallel token generation (many tokens at once), speedometer (latency), and quality check (final-output discriminative loss).
paper_title: T3D: Few-Step Diffusion Language Models via Trajectory Self-Distillation with Direct Discriminative Optimization
paper_authors: Tunyu Zhang, Xinxi Zhang, Ligong Han, Haizhou Shi, Xiaoxiao He
